podcast.title: Space Launch Album Announcement (2021)
podcast.body: The album *Life Forms* was announced in an "interesting way" by launching a renewable capsule filled with hydrogen into space. As the capsule launched, it played a portion of the album's opening track, "I Really Want to Hold You." "A renewable capsule filled with hydrogen was launched into space. And as it was launched, it played a little bit of the album's opening track."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Artistic Re-invention
podcast.body: The formation of Angels & Airwaves represented Tom DeLonge's desire to evolve as an artist, moving away from the "sophomore goofy teenager" persona he had embodied for many years with Blink-182. This new project allowed him to explore different artistic avenues and express a more mature perspective. "it gave Machins to be another type of artist, something away from that sophomore goofy teenager rule that he'd played for so many years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Demos Leak and Rushed Release
podcast.body: The project was initially developed in secret, but its cover was blown when a fan hacked into Tom DeLonge's email, stole five demo tracks, and leaked them online. This forced the band to rush the official release of their debut album. "then some fan hacked into his email and made off with five demos and leaked them online. So with the secret out, the decision was made to rush the release."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Personal Struggles
podcast.body: Angels & Airwaves was formed by Tom DeLonge during Blink-182's hiatus. This period was marked by personal struggles for Tom, including a nervous breakdown attributed to the Blink-182 breakup, a severe back condition, and addiction to painkillers, which affected his clarity of thought. He dedicated months to working on new material in his home studio, teaching himself piano and audio engineering, finding the process therapeutic. "Tom was completely invisible the entire time, Plus 44 was in the news. The breakup of Blink caused what he'd later call a nervous breakdown."

podcast.title: Formation by Tom (Post-Blink 182)
podcast.body: Tom formed this band after quitting Blink 182, and it "did okay." "He went off and formed Angels and Airwaves, which did okay."

podcast.title: Political and Utopian Philosophy
podcast.body: Angels & Airwaves' philosophy was deeply influenced by Tom DeLonge's engagement with politics, sparked by his endorsement of John Kerry for president and his opposition to the Iraq War (where his brother was deployed), alongside his father's leukemia diagnosis. The band adopted a strong streak of utopianism and positivity, with their motto being "Friends and Family First, Band Seconds," reflecting Tom's personal priorities. "Tom became committed to the idea of reform, and the work it would take to make this a better world. And this became baked into the philosophy of this band, Angels, and Airwaves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Prolific Multimedia Output
podcast.body: Since his departure from Blink-182, Tom DeLonge has been highly productive, releasing seven Angels & Airwaves projects, many of which are integral parts of larger multimedia endeavors. These include albums accompanied by animated films, EPs linked to novels co-authored by him, and concepts that extend into documentary series, demonstrating his broad creative scope. "There are now seven angels and airwaves releases."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Unfulfilled Movie Promise
podcast.body: Following the release of their debut album, Tom DeLonge expressed significant satisfaction with Angels & Airwaves' initial output and promised fans a "mind blowing full length movie" in addition to new music. However, this full-length film project never materialized. "he promised that in addition to more new music there would be some kind of mind blowing full length movie. We never saw the movie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation During Blink 182 Hiatus (Post-2005)
xref.body: This band was formed by Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker during Blink 182's indefinite hiatus, a period when Mark Hoppus and Tom DeLonge were not speaking. It was one of several solo/side projects that emerged during that time. "Bands like Tom's Angels and Airwaves and Mark and Travis's Plus 44."

xref.title: Political Activism
xref.body: Tom DeLonge became actively involved in politics, endorsing John Kerry for president and campaigning on the election circuit for a period. His political engagement stemmed from a desire for reform after four years of George Bush's presidency, deeply influencing the philosophical underpinnings of his band, Angels & Airwaves. "He endorsed John Kerry for president. He got sucked into politics. He even toured the election circuit for a while."
